instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: Independent power producer operating a portfolio of 12 solar photovoltaic plants and 3 onshore wind farms across Iberia with a combined capacity of 180 MW. Selling electricity through PPAs and spot market. Evaluating battery storage co-location and AI-driven production forecasting. A growing organization that has moved past founder-led decision-making but is still building the formal processes and governance structures needed to scale. We have some digital tools in place but integration between systems is ad-hoc. Innovation is championed by 1-2 internal advocates.
answers.pastInitiatives: We experimented with a customer self-service portal two years ago after seeing competitors offer similar functionality. We built an MVP with an external agency in 3 months, but customer adoption was disappointing — only 8% of customers created accounts. We did not invest enough in understanding whether our specific customer base actually wanted self-service before building.
answers.strategicGoals: Targeting 30% year-over-year top-line growth. We see untapped demand in adjacent customer segments and are evaluating whether to build, buy, or partner to accelerate market penetration. The core question is whether to deepen our vertical specialization or broaden horizontally into related product categories.
answers.additionalContext: The company is currently facing increasing pressure from large utility incumbents and volatile energy prices across the Iberian market. Management needs to rapidly formalize its operational structure to handle projected growth in renewable assets.
answers.teamSize: Our team includes 3 backend developers, 1 frontend developer, and 1 QA engineer, managed by the CTO who also acts as product owner. We outsource UI/UX design to a freelance designer as needed. The team can handle incremental product improvements but struggles to carve out focused time for larger innovation bets without compromising current sprint commitments.

opportunities.title: Advanced Grid Optimization via Predictive AI
opportunities.rationale: Implementing sophisticated AI for production forecasting and dynamic load balancing can drastically reduce operational costs and improve market response times compared to current manual methods. This move positions Element as a tech-forward leader, attracting better talent.

first_actions: Conduct feasibility study on Python/ML stack integration with existing SCADA data.
Identify 3 pilot projects for AI forecasting in the next quarter.
resources_needed: Internal training workshop for data science basics
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction of forecasted production variance by 15% within 6 months
milestones: Q1: Proof-of-Concept model deployed in sandbox environment
Q2: Pilot deployment on one wind farm using AI predictions

opportunities.title: Tiered Customer Self-Service Portal Enhancement
opportunities.rationale: Since the initial self-service MVP failed adoption, focusing on a smaller, highly valuable segment (e.g., PPAs) with enhanced features like detailed performance dashboards will improve user engagement and data collection.

first_actions: Run targeted UX research with 10 key PPA clients.
Implement a phased rollout of basic tracking and reporting tools.
resources_needed: Internal time from 1 backend developer for integration mapping
execution_plan.success_metric: Achieve 30% adoption rate among targeted PPA segment within 9 months
milestones: Q2: Finalize and deploy enhanced dashboard features.
Q3: Establish formal feedback loop with the internal advocacy team.

next_steps.action: Form a cross-functional 'Growth Innovation Task Force' to prioritize and scope the AI forecasting project.
Define technical requirements for the Tiered Customer Self-Service enhancements based on Q3 research findings.

key_weaknesses: Lack of standardized, formal innovation governance processes leading to inconsistent project prioritization.
High dependence on informal champions rather than embedded innovation culture or structured R&D spend.
Low digital maturity (Level 1) resulting in ad-hoc system integrations that hinder data utilization for predictive modeling.
Strict budget limitations (5%) severely constrain the capacity to test large, high-risk radical projects.
